paper_sections.title: ‘Put on your poker face’: neural systems supporting the anticipation for expressive suppression and cognitive reappraisal
fMRI data pre-processing and general linear model analysis

description.value: The study investigated neural correlates of proactively preparing to use expressive suppression or cognitive reappraisal before viewing negative, high-arousing images, as well as neural activity during the subsequent emotion-regulation period.

design.value: Event-related functional magnetic resonance imaging was recorded in 42 female participants during an emotion-regulation paradigm with suppress, reappraise and appraise trials. Each trial included a preparatory cue followed by a negative image and a success rating.

description.value: Participants rated how successful they were in regulating or appraising their negative emotions, from 1 = not at all to 4 = very good.
Participants rated how they felt while looking at the pictures using a 9-point scale from unhappy to happy.
Participants rated arousal while looking at the pictures using a 9-point scale from calm to excited.
Structured interview used to screen for psychiatric disorders and psychiatric history based on Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fourth Edition, Text Revision criteria.

source_definition.value: The cue instructed participants to suppress, reappraise or appraise their emotions.
The model contained separate regressors for the cue phase and target phase.
Movement parameters were included to account for variance associated with head motion.

description.value: A group of 42 female participants recruited through postings on the university website.

inclusion_criteria.value: without medical conditions that might influence the interpretation of brain functioning related to emotion and cognitive processing

medical_condition.value: without medical conditions that might influence the interpretation of brain functioning related to emotion and cognitive processing

diagnostic_system.value: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fourth Edition, Text Revision

task_description.value: Participants were cued to suppress, reappraise or appraise a series of 63 randomly intermixed trials in three blocks. Each trial began with a fixation cross, followed by a cue word, a preparatory blank-screen period, a negative high-arousing image presented for 10 s, a success rating and an 8-s RELAX period.

instructions.value: For suppression, participants were trained to suppress displaying their feelings elicited by the picture. For reappraisal, they were trained to reinterpret the situational event depicted by changing the emotions, actions and outcomes of individuals depicted in that situational context. For appraisal, they were instructed to simply look at the pictures, feel their natural feelings and not change anything.

stimuli.value: 63 negative pictures of the IAPS with mean arousal values >6 and mean valence ratings <4, based on normative ratings of female participants.

task_performance_measures.value: success rating for regulating or appraising negative emotions

instrument.value: 3T Magnetom Trio MRI scanner system (Siemens Medical Systems, Erlangen, Germany) using an eight-channel radiofrequency head coil

description.value: High-resolution anatomical images were acquired using a T1-weighted 3D Magnetization Prepared RApid Gradient Echo (3D MPRAGE) sequence.

instrument.value: 3T Magnetom Trio MRI scanner system (Siemens Medical Systems, Erlangen, Germany) using an eight-channel radiofrequency head coil

description.value: Whole-brain functional images were collected using a T2*-weighted echo planar imaging sequence sensitive to BOLD contrast.

The first four volumes of all EPI series were excluded. Data processing included slice-time correction, realignment, co-registration, normalization to the MNI template, resampling and spatial smoothing. Low-frequency drifts were removed using discrete cosine functions with a 128-s cut-off.

steps.value: The first four EPI volumes were excluded.
EPI datasets were realigned using rigid body transformations.
The structural image was co-registered with the mean EPI image.
The structural image was normalized to the Montreal Neurological Institute template.
Normalization parameters were applied to the EPI images.
Anatomical image volumes were resampled to 1 × 1 × 1 mm3.
An 8-mm full-width at half maximum filter was used.
Low-frequency drifts were removed with discrete cosine functions using a 128-s cut-off.

hrf_model.value: canonical hemodynamic response function and its temporal derivative

model_settings.value: Separate regressors modeled Cue Suppression, Reappraisal and Appraise during the 1–9 s cue period; Suppression, Reappraisal and Appraise during the 10-s target phase; and the response to the rating screen. The jitter was not separately modeled. Movement parameters were included as covariates.

level.value: subject-level statistical analyses followed by group-level random effects analysis

software.value: SPM5 software (Wellcome Department of Cognitive Neurology, London, UK)

model_settings.value: The precentral gyrus region of interest during Target Suppression was anatomically defined by means of the WFU PickAtlas and comprised the entire precentral gyrus. Beta values were extracted for each participant.

description.value: Participants prepared not to show their feelings on an outward level and then suppressed displaying feelings elicited by the picture.
Participants prepared to down-regulate their emotions and reinterpreted the situational event depicted by changing the emotions, actions and outcomes of individuals in the context.
Participants simply looked at the pictures, felt their natural feelings and did not change anything.
The cue word appeared for 1 s followed by a blank screen lasting 1–9 s, enabling participants to prepare for the instructed emotion-regulation strategy.
A negative, high-arousing image appeared for 10 s while participants performed the emotion regulation or appraisal specified by the prior instructional cue.
